entities.summary:
Jean de Marigny (jean-de-marigny) was a French bishop, younger brother of Enguerrand de Marigny, who played a significant role in the medieval religious landscape of Western Europe.





 As a cleric, Jean de Marigny was involved in the establishment of several churches and monasteries, including the construction of the magnificent Saint-Pierre Church in Chartres, which became a model for ecclesiastical architecture during the Middle Ages. 





 His religious influence extended beyond his immediate diocese, as he collaborated with other prominent clergy and leaders of the Catholic Church to shape doctrine and policy.





 The legacy of Jean de Marigny can be seen in the lasting impact of his religious and architectural endeavors on the development of Western Christianity, particularly in the regions of France and Europe where his influence was most pronounced.





 'The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing' (Psalm 23:1), a quote often attributed to Jean de Marigny, reflects his unwavering devotion to his faith and his commitment to serving the Church.
